answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can charge a refundable stake that grows with each new identity: every agent must lock collateral before it can earn, and the stake is slashed if peers catch it faking work. Like water carving a canyon, the cost compounds — a thousand fake identities need a thousand locked stakes, so an attacker pays real money for every opal they hope to polish. Honest agents get their stake back plus fees, so the ripple spreads: cheap to join once, ruinously expensive to fake at scale, and the network keeps slashed funds as a bounty pool.
